artworks.title: Phosphorus and Hesperus
artworks.description: De Morgan’s Pre-Raphaelite pair: Phosphorus (Eosphorus), the Morning Star, clasps Hesperus, the Evening Star — Hesiod’s dawn-bringer as a luminous youth, not the Christian Satan who later borrowed Lucifer’s Latin name.

popCulture.title: Theogony (Eosphorus)
popCulture.creator: Hesiod
popCulture.description: Hesiod’s Eosphorus — Dawn-bringer, child of Eos and Astraeus — is the Morning Star among the winds and stars that crown heaven.

popCulture.title: Phosphorus (morning star)
popCulture.description: Greek Phosphorus / Latin Lucifer as the personified Morning Star — Venus at dawn — carefully distinct from later Christian demonology that reused the Latin name.
